source.title: Understanding prompt engineering does not require rethinking generalization
source.authors: Victor Akinwande; Yi-Ding Jiang; Dylan Sam; J. Kolter

record.tranche_reason: Tests prompt models’ generalization and their ability to fit randomly flipped labels, arguing that this behavior differs from conventional deep networks that can fit random labels. The study concerns prompts on pretrained vision-language models, not the listed standard-training neural network settings.
record.gate_note: Own experiments report greedy prompt search on natural and randomly flipped labels, plus prompt-length and data/vocabulary sensitivity. The random-label results are described in text, but the plots do not supply recoverable numeric values. Other model-generalization claims discussed in the introduction or references are not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study tests discrete prompt search over frozen pretrained CLIP models, not the coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the neural-network training recipes named in V1. Failure of this restricted search procedure to fit random labels does not test those networks' memorization capacity. No results test V2–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate but needs the authors' explicit limitation: language-model-prior PAC-Bayes bounds explain generalization of discrete prompt selection conditional on a useful pretrained vision-language model, not the underlying model's own generalization. They report little prompt-search overfitting and contrast its failure to fit random labels with conventional neural-network training.
record.recipe_differences: Greedy discrete prompt search over pretrained CLIP representations, with LLaMA-7B used as a prior for bounds; not standard gradient training of neural network weights.
record.method_sensitivity: Prompt length: the generalization gap increases with prompt length, though the text says there is little overfitting even at the longest lengths. Random-label fit is examined as the flip ratio varies.

fits_no_version.finding: With prompt length fixed at five, Greedy fails to fit random labels across CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, fMoW and OfficeHome; exact error values are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restricted discrete prompt search over pretrained vision-language models can resist fitting label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Greedy achieves natural-label train/test errors of 0.050/0.060 and 0.023/0.028 on CIFAR-10, and 0.208/0.255 and 0.142/0.180 on CIFAR-100, for CLIP ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Discrete prompt search over pretrained CLIP can achieve strong held-out classification performance with modest train–test gaps.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2023 Workshop: Sampling and Optimization in Discrete Space (SODS 2023)
record.problems: The findings concern discrete prompt search on pretrained vision-language models, not networks trained from scratch with standard gradient methods. Random-label results are described qualitatively and shown in plots without recoverable exact values. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the result rows.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the specified neural-network architectures and training recipes; random-label held-out performance under those recipes. CLIP's underlying training and generalization are explicitly outside the analysis.
Network width beyond the zero-training-error threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and sensitivity to optimizer tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both proposed V1 verdicts. The contrast with conventional neural networks concerns a different hypothesis class and optimization procedure, so it neither supports nor limits V1. The corrected row states indicate inability to determine a listed version, not uncertainty about the authors' qualitative prompt-search findings.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the same architectures and standard training recipes as Zhang et al.; tests greedy prompt search using pretrained CLIP on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, fMoW and OfficeHome. Does not report the specified Inception, AlexNet or MLP experiments.

rows.check: The qualitative result is accurately reported, but measures five-token prompt search rather than neural-network weight training. Its failure to fit corrupted labels cannot establish a partial or absent V1 effect.

reader_labels.label: supports
